title: Gemini 4 Argon for Robotics
key_facts: Google says Gemini 4 Argon scores 87% on the Embodied Reasoning (ERQA) benchmark, a test of physical and spatial problem-solving in 3D scenes, 'outperforming every other frontier model'.
Examples include Argon controlling a Boston Dynamics Spot quadruped to learn to step on a foot-pedal bin, after practising in a simulated digital twin.
Argon writes physics simulations, builds digital twins from robot teleoperation video and labels robot video, including a 136-second origami-folding episode.

Starting from one photo of a tabletop, Argon built a simulation and collected 4,500+ simulated episodes, which Google says raised a real robot's success rate from 56% to 75% and cut completion time from 35 s to 24 s.
Google calls Argon a step toward 'physical AGI' and says developers can build with it today on Google's developer platforms.
All results are from Google's own post; no independent testing is reported.
quote_evidence: Using pure reasoning, Argon scores 87%, outperforming every other frontier model.
Argon controls a Boston Dynamics Spot® quadruped (12-DoF legs + 6-DoF arm) to learn a new skill: stepping on a foot-pedal trash bin to throw away soda cans.

Starting from a single RGB photo of the real tabletop, Argon autonomously builds a calibrated MuJoCo simulation twin, defines new tasks, and synthesizes a closed-loop motion generator to collect 4,500+ domain-randomized episodes in simulation—boosting real-world physical robot Success Rate from 56% to 75% and reducing completion time from 35s to 24s.
why_it_matters_hint: A leading AI model is pitched as a robot's reasoning and training engine, but the numbers are Google's own.
notes: Google's own developer post; every benchmark and demo result is a company claim.
